features.name: Fluent Design Language
features.description: Microsoft's official design language used for all Microsoft products. Provides comprehensive style guides, widgets, colors, icons and interaction paradigms to ensure consistency across Microsoft products including Business Central.
caveats: Business Central applies its own treatment and patterns while adhering to Fluent standards
Not all Office paradigms directly apply to ERP tasks

features.name: Figma for UI Design
features.description: The design tool used by Business Central design team for creating UI mockups and designs. Recently acquired by Adobe. Provides multi-user editing capabilities allowing design teams to collaborate on the same document simultaneously. CSS can be taken directly from Figma for developer handoff.
caveats: Recently acquired by Adobe
Initial mockups often differ significantly from final implementation
CSS handoff improves developer workflow

features.name: Company Switcher
features.description: A feature that allows users to switch between different companies in Business Central. Described as a smaller feature with a shorter development timeline from concept to release compared to larger investments. Evolved from a simple company switcher to a complex environment and company switcher. Initial design was a simple company dropdown, but user feedback revealed customers needed to switch between multiple environments and companies across environments.
caveats: Originally designed as simple company switcher, expanded scope significantly
Requires coordination between platform and client teams
Involved aligning with Microsoft product patterns from other platforms

features.name: Onboarding Project
features.description: A multi-release investment feature that was gradually built out over multiple releases. Required a lengthy period of research, design and implementation to understand what onboarding means for Business Central users. Includes optional banner-based onboarding checklist that users can engage with or dismiss. Replaced an earlier full-screen modal approach that was too invasive and required completion before users could explore Business Central.
caveats: Took multiple releases to research, design and implement
Replaced an earlier full-screen modal design that was rejected
Requires extreme discoverability for users with no Business Central knowledge

features.name: Analysis mode
features.description: A feature designed for experienced Business Central users to perform data analysis. Initially mocked with tabs at the bottom of the page, but user testing revealed users overlooked them, so tabs were moved to the top of the page before shipping.
caveats: Targeting experienced users only, not new users

features.name: Prompt dialogue for Copilot features
features.description: An AI feature that started in V1 as very limited but has been continually built out. Now provides the foundation for delivering Copilot actions and features in Business Central.
caveats: V1 was limited, has been iterated upon

features.name: Design Specification with Red Lines
features.description: A detailed design specification approach using Figma that documents precise details including font sizes, margin sizes, spacing, and component behavior. Features red line annotations showing the design intent that developers must implement. Includes testing for content expansion and localization impacts.
caveats: Includes testing for content expansion and localization impacts
Requires flexibility for multi-language scaling

features.name: Component Flexibility for Localization
features.description: Design components are built with flexibility to scale up or down based on localized content, ensuring that text flows and looks reasonable across multiple languages without redesign.
caveats: Design challenge due to unknown content length at design time

features.name: Partner UI Limitations and Standardization
features.description: Partners and developers building extensions for Business Central have limited UI control. They cannot adjust pixels, button sizes, or element placement. Microsoft makes centralized UI decisions to ensure consistency and provide built-in functionality like behavior, translations, and security.
caveats: Partners must stay within the standard flexibility spectrum
Building highly customized solutions outside Business Central standards becomes complicated

features.name: Power Apps Integration for Customization
features.description: Power Apps can be used as an alternative when Business Central customization needs exceed the flexibility spectrum. This allows building highly customized solutions while maintaining integration with Business Central data.
caveats: Power Apps requires more development effort than using Business Central standard pages
Requires evaluating tradeoff between flexibility and built-in functionality
